checks.label: Valves can share one symbol, with the notes and legend telling what the symbol alone cannot: every valve on the air sheet is drawn alike, and only V7 and V8, marked N.C., are shut as drawn
A one line typically starts at the top with the incoming power and its disconnecting device: the first switchboard does, while the second has both supplies below its busbars and its loads above them
Each symbol is drawn in its normal condition: at rest every normally closed contact on the hoist sheet is closed, every normally open one is open, and no coil is in

Isolation points on the plant should match the line diagram: the plant has one valve the sheet does not show, so with V3 shut the plant's users keep air through it, the hose point and, back through V6, the rest of the header, while the sheet shows every user without air
Both compressors stopped: every user keeps air from R1 until its needle falls to the low mark, then all three stop; with V3 shut instead, all three stop at once and R1 stays full
Second board: 2 sources (slips 1 and 3); as run, section 2 is fed through -Q8; with -Q8 open, -M6 and -E6 stop and -M5 and -E5 run
Hoist: from mid-travel Up raises the hook; at the top Up does nothing and Down still lowers it; with -S10 open neither works

Isolating R1: V1, V2 and V3 cut it off from both compressors and the header; V3 alone leaves the compressors feeding it; V1 and V2 alone leave it feeding the header; opening V7 would join its inlet line to the header
First board: -Q23 cannot close while -Q13 is closed; with -Q13 open and -Q23 closed, -M3 is still fed, from -G2 through section B
The upright stands 60 − 10 = 50 mm above the base (slips 60 and 70), and the typed fields ask exactly these
Before an answer nothing gives it away: every puzzle opens on its own sheet as drawn, with no tabs, rings, marks or locks
Every demonstration settles within 4.5 s, and every answer plays out within 5 s
